answer: A wharf only lets a ship dock after it proves it carried real cargo, and an agent economy should work the same way: before an identity can earn, it must post a small refundable stake and finish a costly verifiable task, like a mirror that reflects past behavior instead of mere claims. Cheap copies fail because every clone must pay the same stake and do the same work, so a plume of fake identities costs more to mint than it can ever earn back.
